rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that several checks are carried out one after another on separate components, and that a later joint step follows only if every check succeeds, while a failed check sends the work back to be redone: Model one exclusive decision gateway after the last check and before the joint step. Route one branch, labelled with the condition that all checks passed, to the joint step. Route the other branch, labelled with the failure condition, to a rework task that loops back to the building step the description names. Do not connect the joint step directly from the checks, and do not omit the gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that several checks are carried out one after another on separate components, and that a later joint step follows only if every check succeeds, while a failed check sends the work back to be redone

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the actor gives or hands over items to another party, and that party then performs work on those items before the process continues: Model the hand-over as its own manual task placed after the step that precedes it and before the task in which the other party performs the work. Connect the preceding task to the hand-over task and the hand-over task to the work task with sequence flows. Do not drop the hand-over, and do not connect the preceding task directly to the other party's work task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the actor gives or hands over items to another party, and that party then performs work on those items before the process continues

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that each unit produced by a production step must be checked separately before the units are combined, and that a unit failing its check is reworked and checked again: Model one separate test task for each unit that the description says must be checked before combining, placed directly after the step that produces that unit and before the joint step. Each unit gets its own test task, not one shared test. Route each test's outcome through an exclusive gateway: the success branch continues toward the joint step, and the failure branch leads to a rework task for that same unit, which loops back to the test. Do not omit a test the description states, and do not connect a production step directly to the joint step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that each unit produced by a production step must be checked separately before the units are combined, and that a unit failing its check is reworked and checked again

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that several built units make up a product, that each unit must be checked on its own after it is built, and that a joint step follows only if every check succeeds: Model a separate check task for every unit the description names. Place each check after the build of its own unit, and order the checks as the description states, or in parallel if it gives no order. If the description gives no count, model the build-and-check pair once per unit it describes, and use a loop only when the description states a repetition. Do not replace the per-unit checks with one generic check task. After the last check, place one exclusive decision. Route its all-passed branch to the joint step and its failure branch to a rework task that returns to the build step the description names. Do not connect the joint step directly from the checks.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that several built units make up a product, that each unit must be checked on its own after it is built, and that a joint step follows only if every check succeeds
